title: The saddle trigger ends with "Repeat this process once", so one attack makes two attacking copies of whichever nonlegendary creature saddled it, doubling that creature's enter-the-battlefield trigger.
summary: A budget mono-red build is organised around the second half of the attack trigger, which runs the copy process twice rather than once. Because the commander has haste it can be cast, saddled with a cheap enter-the-battlefield creature and attack on the same turn, doubling that trigger immediately for mana, cards, removal or damage. The copy only happens for a nonlegendary saddler, which pushes the creature base toward cheap repeatable enter triggers instead of marquee legends.

notes: The primer names the exact rules clause the build hangs on and explains why haste makes it work the turn the commander lands.
From a channel that specialises in overlooked commanders, which is the targeting signal docs/SOURCES.md describes.

alternatives.name: Saddling with legendary bombs
alternatives.reason: The trigger only copies a nonlegendary creature that saddled it, so a legendary saddler produces nothing at all.

alternatives.name: Building it as a go-wide token board
alternatives.reason: The copies are sacrificed at the beginning of the next end step, so value has to be banked the same turn rather than accumulated.
